# Code Principles

## Core: "Code is not an asset, it is a liability"
The asset is the behavior. Code is the cost. Every line must be read, understood, debugged, updated, and can break.

## Reduction Rules
- Delete unused code — Git has history.
- Delete commented-out code.
- When a feature is superseded, delete old code in the same PR.
- Actively hunt dead code when touching a file.
- Prefer deleting lines over adding lines when behavior stays the same.

## Abstraction & Duplication
- Extract on first duplication (2 call sites = extract).
- Don't add helpers "in case we need them."
- Don't add config options for flexibility — hardcode, add the option when the second use case arrives.

## Error Handling
- Only validate at system boundaries (user input, API responses, DB reads). Trust internal code.
- Don't handle edge cases that can't currently happen — add handling when the case becomes real.

## Comments
- Minimal comments only when completely necessary. Code should be self-explanatory.
- Never comment-out code. Never explain WHAT code does — the code itself should say that.

## Naming
- Named constants over magic numbers/strings, always — even single-use. The name IS the documentation.
- Boolean prefixes: `is`, `has`, `can`, `should` (e.g. `isLoading`, `hasPermission`, `canEdit`).
- Descriptive names for unused params (`_unusedEvent` over `_`).

## Style
- `const`-first — use `let` only when reassignment is needed.
- Early returns / guard clauses — avoid deep nesting.
- Ternary ONLY for simple value assignment (`const x = cond ? a : b`). Everything else uses if/else.
- Direct imports — no barrel files (index.ts re-exports).

## Size Limits
- File: ~800 lines max → refactor is imminent.
- Function/method: ~35 lines max → extract.

## Design
- Apply SOLID and DRY. Use design patterns where they offer utility.

## Folder Architecture ("Use the app → find the code")
The folder tree mirrors UI navigation. Using the app once = knowing where code lives.

```
src/app/
├── pages/           ← one folder per navigable page (flat siblings, no admin/ nesting)
│   └── {page}/
│       ├── {sub-page}/   ← sub-pages as subfolders (e.g. chat/, tasks/)
│       ├── helpers/      ← page-specific services (only used by this page)
│       ├── dialogs/      ← page-specific dialogs
├── services/        ← multi-page services (used by 2+ pages)
│   ├── auth/        ← auth, profile, guards
│   ├── data/        ← firestore facades (user, project, donor...)
│   └── ui/          ← right-panel, dialog-back, mobile-sidebar, title...
├── components/      ← reusable UI (shared components, directives, pipes)
├── models/          ← all interfaces/types grouped by domain (project.model, donor.model...)
```

**Rules:**
- Service used only by its page → `pages/{page}/helpers/`
- Used by 2+ pages → `services/`
- All models in top-level `models/` (dependency arrow: pages → services → models)
- No admin/ grouping — all pages are flat siblings in pages/
- Reusable UI components → `components/`

> Feature-specific pitfalls have been moved to the relevant `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` files (angular-components, mobile, chat, cloud-functions, testing). Only universal items remain here.

## Behavioral
- **NEVER run recursive PowerShell scripts** like `Get-ChildItem -Recurse | ForEach-Object { Get-Content ... }` — this instantly freezes VS Code. Use `grep_search`, `file_search`, or `read_file` tools instead. Also avoid `Select-String -Recurse` on large trees.
- **E2E tests must show live progress**: Never pipe Playwright output to `Out-String` or use `mode=sync`. Always use `mode=async` so the user sees real-time progress in the terminal.
- **Never hallucinate about external apps.** Say "I don't know" if unsure.
- **Never claim to have "checked the internet"** unless actually fetching a webpage.
- **Ask mobile or desktop first** before debugging layout/alignment issues.
- **Don't auto-update docs** — user confirms via `/update-docs` prompt.
- **Always deploy after code changes** — never leave changes undeployed. Build + `firebase deploy --only hosting --force` immediately after every code edit.
- **Revert failed attempts in the SAME deploy as the fix.**
- **One hypothesis at a time.** Max 3 attempts of the same category — then switch approach.

## E2E / Playwright
- **WebKit CI needs Playwright container**: Use `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.60.0-noble` container for reliable WebKit deps. Standard ubuntu-latest has incomplete WebKit support.
- **WebKit Touch/ContextMenu in mobile emulation**: Playwright's WebKit with iPhone emulation can't construct `Touch()`/`TouchEvent()` (Illegal constructor) and `dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('contextmenu'))` doesn't trigger Angular bindings. Context menu tests must `test.skip()` on WebKit via `'none'` return from `openMobileContextMenu()`. Real iPhones use native touch — this is a Playwright limitation, not an app bug.
- **Hover action buttons intercepted by adjacent messages**: Fixed via `z-index: 3` on `.message:hover` in `chat.component.scss` — creates stacking context so hover action buttons aren't intercepted by adjacent messages. No `force: true` needed. Must be > 2 (reactions-row z-index) so the emoji picker inside the hovered message stays above other messages' reaction chips.
- **Stacking context traps child z-index values**: When a parent has `z-index` (creating a stacking context), ALL descendants' z-index values are trapped within it. The emoji picker (`z-index: 1000`) inside `.message:hover { z-index: 1 }` was rendered BELOW adjacent reactions (`z-index: 2`) because 1 < 2 in the parent context. Fix: ensure message hover z-index > reactions z-index.
- **`isolation: isolate` causes hover paint loops**: Adding `isolation: isolate` to `main` (grid container) while `.message:hover` toggles z-index creates rapid repaint cycles — the stacking context boundary triggers relayout on each hover frame. Use `position: relative; z-index: 0` on `:host` (app-root) instead for defense-in-depth against CDK overlay competition.
- **Scroll assertions after async operations need polling, not fixed waits**: ResizeObserver + Angular rendering race means `waitForTimeout(500)` is unreliable for scroll position checks. Use `waitForFunction(() => el.scrollHeight - el.scrollTop - el.clientHeight < threshold, null, { timeout: 5000 })`.
- **Scroll-to-bottom button click needs waitForScrollStable**: The button click triggers a `scrollTo` with `behavior: 'smooth'` — measuring `scrollTop` immediately after gives stale values (gap = 8587px instead of <150). Always add `waitForScrollStable()` (RAF-based `scrollTop` convergence check) after programmatic scroll before asserting position.
- **Scroll-to-top in beforeEach needs retry loop**: Real-time Firestore listeners may auto-scroll back to bottom after `scrollTop = 0`. Use a loop that sets `scrollTop = 0`, waits 1s, checks gap, and repeats up to 5 times.
- **@mention popup shows raw UIDs before userNameMap resolves**: Add a `waitForTimeout(500)` before typing filter text, and don't assert on specific user names that depend on async data loading.
- **Textarea highlight overlay jump**: When adding a backdrop div behind a transparent textarea for styled text (e.g. bold mentions), do NOT apply `position: relative; z-index; background: transparent` unconditionally to the textarea — only apply when the overlay is active (e.g. via `.has-mention-overlay` class). Unconditional styles shift the text rendering layout. Also: `overflow: hidden` on the popup container overrides `overflow-y: auto` — so scrolling won't work even if `max-height` is set.

## Testing
- **AngularFire JIT errors in unit tests**: If a spec imports a module that transitively imports `@angular/fire/firestore`, the Angular unit-test builder throws JIT compilation errors. Fix: extract pure functions (e.g. `getLang`, `getLocale`) into a dependency-free file (`active-lang.ts`) and import from there. Don't try `vi.mock` for relative imports — the builder blocks it.
- **Angular test builder blocks `vi.mock` for relative imports**: The `@angular/build:unit-test` vitest-mock-patch rejects `vi.mock('./relative-path')`. ## Firestore Queries
- **Async recompute races with navigation**: `recomputeUnread()` checks `recentlyVisited` at the start, but the async `computeUnreadCount()` call takes a network round-trip. - **DM list must use `trackEntity()` like projects/skills**: Manual dual subscriptions (latestMessage$ + readState$) miss the `getActiveId` guard that prevents recomputing unread for the currently-viewed conversation. Always use `UnreadTrackingService.trackEntity()` for all three sections.

Fix: query with a rule-satisfying constraint (`where("members", "array-contains", uid)`) and filter the other field client-side. Admin/manager can use the direct query.
- **System messages after membership removal fail silently**: If a client posts a system message (via `postSystemMessage` callable) AFTER removing itself from `members[]`, the callable rejects with `permission-denied` (membership check fails). Fix: use a Firestore trigger (`onDocumentWritten`) on the parent doc that detects member array diffs and posts messages server-side with admin privileges. Fix: (1) use raw snapshot doc count (before client-side `deletedFor` filtering), (2) in steady state, re-enable `hasMoreOlder = true` whenever a snapshot fills the query window (`msgs.length >= PAGE_SIZE`). - **Non-overflowing initial load blocks pagination permanently**: The anchor strategy (`startWithAnchor`) loads only `CONTEXT_SIZE = 10` messages before `lastReadAt`. ## Cloud Functions
- **User name resolution must prefer `displayName`**: The `displayName` field is the user's chosen name (set during onboarding — could be a nickname like "Zumi" or a properly formatted full name like "Kovács Nóra" for Hungarian). Never prefer `firstName` — it's just the given name without language-aware ordering. Priority: `displayName` → `firstName` → `'Unknown'`.
- **Rate limit off-by-one pattern**: When a Firestore transaction returns the current count and the outer code checks `current > limit`, the limit is never hit (e.g., limit=5, count reaches 5, `5 > 5` is false). Use `>=` for "at limit" checks after increment-based transactions.
- **Invite-style single-use tokens need transactions**: Any read-then-write pattern where two concurrent callers could both read the "unused" state and both proceed must use `db.runTransaction()`. Without it, both succeed and the last write wins.
- **Find-or-create patterns need deterministic IDs or transactions**: A `findConversation()` → `createConversation()` two-step with auto-generated IDs is a TOCTOU race. - **Storage triggers must match bucket region**: `onObjectFinalized` must have `{ region: 'us-east1' }` (or whichever region the bucket is in). Mismatched regions cause deploy failure.

Wrap each operation with `.catch(e => logger.error(...))` so failures are logged but don't crash the trigger.

## CSS Grid
- **Single-column grid with multiple items targeting same column**: When `grid-template-columns` collapses to `1fr` (e.g. `.no-nav` mode) and multiple items have `grid-column: 1` without explicit `grid-row`, CSS Grid auto-places them into separate rows. Images can keep fade-in.
- **OnPush `uiTick` must propagate through ALL component layers**: If `ChatComponent` (Default CD) passes `[uiTick]` to `MessageBubbleComponent` (OnPush), but `MessageBubbleComponent` doesn't forward it to `TextBubbleComponent` (also OnPush), the inner component NEVER re-checks when `uiTick` changes — its inputs (`msg`, `host`) are the same references. Always chain `[uiTick]` through every OnPush layer that reads host state (like `host.getReadReceipts()`). Symptom: "seen" avatars take 60+ seconds to appear (waiting for unrelated CD trigger).
- **Race between `readState` subscription and `userNameMap$`**: The readState `collectionData` listener and the `users$` collection listener are independent Firestore queries. If readState arrives first, `userNameMap` is empty → avatars have no `photoURL`. Must call `refreshNames()` (rebuild readStates from rawReadStates) when userNameMap/userPhotoMap update, plus `tickAndDetect()` to push to OnPush children.
- **Production minification strips `if (!x) return` guards**: Angular's production optimizer can remove null-check early-return guards in component methods if the template types suggest null isn't possible. Use **optional chaining** (`task?.createdBy`) instead — `?.` compiles to a null-check that minifiers cannot strip.
- **`MatNativeDateModule` in standalone components**: Don't import `MatNativeDateModule` — it doesn't reliably provide `DateAdapter` in standalone components after tree-shaking. Use `provideNativeDateAdapter()` in `providers` instead. All datepicker components must follow this pattern.
- **Bare text in `<mat-form-field>`**: Never use bare `{{ ... | transloco }}` for labels or errors inside `<mat-form-field>`. Wrap labels in `<mat-label>`, errors in `<mat-error>` — bare interpolation renders as unstyled inline text that doesn't float or style as errors. `floatLabel: "always"` has no effect without `<mat-label>`.
- **CSS stacking: `position: relative` sibling paints over `static` sibling**: A `position: relative` element paints above a `position: static` sibling, regardless of DOM order. In chat, `.message` had `position: relative` (for hover z-index) and `.read-receipts` was `static` — the bubble painted over the receipt avatars. Fix: add `position: relative` to `.read-receipts` so DOM order determines paint order. General rule: if two siblings overlap (negative margins, absolute children), ensure both have the same `position` type.
- **Fixed `CHARS_PER_LINE` in bubble collapse clips mobile messages**: `ChatBubbleCollapseService` estimated wrapping with a hardcoded 50 chars/line. On mobile, bubbles are ~255px wide (68% of 375px) and fit only ~25 chars/line — the service underestimated line count, didn't trigger "see more", and CSS `overflow-y: clip` silently truncated content. Fix: compute `charsPerLine` dynamically from `window.innerWidth * 0.68 - padding`, capped at 50 for desktop.
- **`overflow-y: clip` + fixed `max-height` clips variable-height content**: `.bubble-content` uses `overflow-y: clip` + `max-height` for collapse animation. When a link preview image or reply quote consumes part of the pixel budget, the "see more" link and text below get silently clipped. Fix: `getMaxHeight(msg)` returns `null` (no CSS max-height) for messages with `linkPreview` or `replyTo` — rely solely on `getTruncatedText` for content limiting.
- **`FIELD_VALIDATORS` includes `required` for location**: The shared `FIELD_VALIDATORS["location"]` preset includes `Validators.required`. - **`mat-icon-button` as `matIconSuffix` adds height to form fields**: A `<button mat-icon-button matIconSuffix>` adds 48px height, making the field taller than adjacent fields using `mat-datepicker-toggle`. Use `<mat-icon matIconSuffix>` instead for compact icons. Put `(click)` on the `<mat-form-field>` so clicking anywhere opens the picker.

- **Drag-then-click in custom scroll wheels**: A `click` event fires after `mouseup` even when the user was dragging. If the wheel has both drag and click-to-select handlers, the click overrides the drag result. Fix: track `wasDragged` (set when movement > 3px), suppress click handler when true.

During hard reset, there's a window where the page is rendered but the class isn't applied — touch input during this gap scrolls `.grid-content` and the scrollTop gets stuck when `:host { overflow: hidden }` later takes effect. Use `:host` styles on the component instead (timing-independent).

No z-index on a regular body-level element (like `.pac-container`) can appear above top-layer elements. Otherwise the popup stays open for the entire network round-trip (feels unresponsive, hover-leave doesn't dismiss because `showEmojiPickerForMsg` keeps the element rendered). Pattern: `this.showPicker = null; await this.doWrite();`.

- **Always `npx tsc` in `functions/`** before deploying Cloud Functions. No predeploy hook.
- **PowerShell**: Quote comma-separated firebase targets: `firebase deploy --only "functions,hosting"`.
- **Always use `--force`** on `firebase deploy` to skip interactive confirmation prompts (e.g. "Would you like to proceed?" when creating new functions). Never let deploy commands hang waiting for input.
- **Deploy storage rules alongside hosting**: `firebase deploy --only hosting` does NOT deploy `storage.rules`. If storage paths were added/changed, always `firebase deploy --only "storage,hosting"`.
- **Storage `allow write` blocks deletes**: `allow write` with `request.resource.size`/`contentType` checks fails for `delete` operations (where `request.resource` is null). Always split into `allow create, update` + separate `allow delete`.
- **JSON imports outside `include` expand `rootDir`**: Fix: set explicit `"rootDir": "."` in tsconfig.
- **CI/CD Firebase Functions IAM**: Service account needs Cloud Functions Developer, Service Account User, Secret Manager Secret Accessor + Viewer, Cloud Scheduler Admin.
- **GCP quota throttling**: When deploying 60+ functions, some may fail. Redeploy failed ones individually.

- **NO BOM in JSON files**: Browsers/Transloco interpret BOM bytes as content → mojibake.
- **Never use PowerShell `Out-File`/`Set-Content` for UTF-8 with diacritics** — use Node.js `fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync`.

- **`authDomain` must match hosting domain** (`web.app`, not `firebaseapp.com`).

- **`intent://` is Android-only**: On iOS, show "Copy link" with Safari instructions.

The toolbar needs `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)` and height must be `calc(base-height + env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px))`. On regular web/PWA, `env(safe-area-inset-top)` resolves to `0px` (no change).
- **Bottom content clipped by gesture nav bar**: Edge-to-edge means the WebView extends behind the Android gesture bar (or 3-button nav bar). `--hm-bottom-nav-height` MUST include `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` — defined as `calc(56px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))`. children.text: > **Type**: Public B2C. Free, open-source utility for the benefit of humanity.

> **Brief**: Users set up alerts that fire when important things happen in the world — breaking news, market movements, natural disasters. Delivered by email and Slack, with a channel abstraction so more channels can be added later. An admin view is required.
> **Document status**: Proposal. User has final word on every decision.
To stay within 24h, we deliberately **cut** these from MVP. They appear on the roadmap, not in MVP.
- Paid data providers (premium stock feeds, Bloomberg, Reuters, USGS enterprise).
- User-submitted RSS feeds (admin-managed only in MVP; user-request flow on roadmap).
- Push notifications, SMS, Discord, Microsoft Teams, webhooks (interface ready, only email + Slack implemented).
- Donations / payments (an "announcement" admin feature is in; payments are not).
- Multi-language UI (English only in MVP; copy lives in i18n keys from day 1 so adding locales is mechanical).
- Mobile app push (web push is a possible post-MVP stretch).
- **Session management**: JWT (access 15m) + refresh token (30d, httpOnly cookie).
- **Profile**: display name, time zone (used to render digest times correctly), preferred language.
- **No social login in MVP.** Hooks in `AuthProvider` interface so Google/Apple can drop in without a schema change.
A 3-choice landing step. Whichever path the user picks, the wizard ends in a populated "My Alerts" dashboard.
| **1. Choose path** | Three options: (a) AI-assisted setup, (b) manual setup, (c) skip → go with sensible defaults. |

| **2a. AI path** | Conversational UI: ~5 short questions ("Which regions matter to you?", "Industries you follow?", "Markets you watch?"). Backend calls `OnboardingAiService` which returns a starter set of alert suggestions. User reviews and accepts/edits. |
| **2b. Manual path** | User lands on alert-builder directly with empty state and the three category tiles (News, Markets, Disasters). |
| **2c. Skip** | User is given 3 default alerts (one of each category) and lands on the dashboard. |
| **3. Channel setup** | User configures at least one channel (email is required; Slack optional). The user can change delivery mode per channel. |
Defaults (path c) ship as a JSON file the admin can edit, so the "skip" path stays curated.
Alerts have a **type** (News, Market, Disaster) and **filters** specific to that type. Each alert has one or more **channel subscriptions** that say "send this alert to channel X in mode Y".
Multi-feature filter. An alert can use any combination of:
- **Per-source subscription**: pick from the admin-curated list of RSS feeds (e.g. Reuters World, BBC Tech, AP Top News). Multiple sources allowed.
- **Keyword filter**: comma-separated keywords with AND/OR modes; case-insensitive; matches against title + summary.
- **Common topic tags**: tags from a curated taxonomy (e.g. `politics`, `ai`, `climate`, `startups`). Multi-select.
- "Describe what you care about" text box on the alert form. Sends to `OnboardingAiService` and returns a suggested filter set the user can accept or modify. Opt-in per alert.
- **% change in time window**: e.g. "AAPL moves 5% within any rolling 1-hour window". Symbol list, threshold %, window length (5m / 15m / 1h / 1d).
Out of scope for MVP: absolute price threshold, volume spike, symbol news. (Roadmap.)

A market alert uses **yfinance** quotes via a Python sidecar (see `2-stack.md`). Quotes are 15-minute delayed. This is documented in the UI ("data delayed up to 15 minutes"). We do **not** promise real-time in MVP.
- **Geographic region**: country list, US state list, or "global". Multiple allowed.
- **Event type**: earthquake, tsunami, hurricane/typhoon, volcano, wildfire, flood.
- **Severity threshold**: per-event-type minimum magnitude/category (e.g. `M5.0+` for earthquake, `Cat 3+` for hurricane). Defaults are sensible.
Data sources: USGS (earthquakes), GDACS (global), NHC (hurricanes). Free, no API key.
A **channel** is a user's connection to an external destination. Each user can have one or more channels:

- **Email**: SMTP target (default = signup email; user can add more). Verified via a **confirmation code sent to the address** — the user pastes the code (or clicks the link) to confirm. We never send real alerts to an unverified address.
- **Slack**: incoming-webhook URL. Verified via a test message on save.

**Quiet hours** (per channel): user can set a start/end time (e.g. "no Slack between 22:00 and 07:00 local"). Real-time matches that fire inside the quiet window are queued and sent at the next allowed moment; digest modes are unaffected. Stored as `Channel.QuietHoursStart` / `Channel.QuietHoursEnd` (nullable; default null = no quiet hours).
- `digest-daily` — batch, once a day at user's chosen hour (default 8am local).
A channel-mode matrix is shown in the alert editor: rows = alerts, columns = channels, cell = mode dropdown.

**Channel abstraction**: a backend `INotificationChannel` interface with `Send(NotificationPayload)` and `Verify(destination)`. Only `EmailChannel` and `SlackChannel` are implemented in MVP. SMS, push, webhook are stubbed but compile. Adding a new channel = one new class + DI registration.
- List of alerts grouped by type (News, Markets, Disasters).
- Per alert: name, filters summary, channel-mode matrix, last fired, toggle on/off, edit, delete.
- Inline **"test this alert"** button: re-runs the matcher with the most recent N events and shows what *would* have fired. Cheap, builds trust, **in MVP** (per resolved decision 2).
- "Activity" tab: a feed of all notifications sent in the last 30 days (resend link, mark as read, view source event).
- Account (name, email, time zone, password change, account deletion).
- Channels (add/remove email addresses, Slack webhooks; verify state; default per-type).
- Notification preferences (default delivery mode per type, quiet hours, daily digest hour).
- API tokens (roadmap; not in MVP — placeholder tab labeled "coming soon" so the nav structure is final).
- **Landing page** with hero, "what is this", "how it works", "supported sources", CTA → sign up. Markdown-backed, build-time generated.

- **Pricing/About**: open-source, no paid tiers. **No donate button in MVP** (per resolved decision 4). If we have spare time near the end of the 24h, a "Support this project" footer link to a placeholder page is acceptable; otherwise omit entirely.
- **Privacy / Terms**: legal pages, generated from markdown at build time. Plain English.
- **Status page** (read-only, from `/api/health` + last-poll timestamps per source).
A separate `/admin` area. Role: `Admin`. Only seeded users with the role can access (bootstrap admin = first user or env var). RBAC implementation details in `2-stack.md`.
- **News sources**: add/edit/remove RSS/Atom feeds. Show last fetch time, last error, fetch count, item count. Manual "fetch now" button.
- **Market symbols**: enable/disable symbols, group into sectors (for the UI to filter by), set market hours (for "during trading hours only" filtering post-MVP).
- **Disaster sources**: enable/disable each upstream (USGS, GDACS, NHC), set default severity thresholds.
Admin-managed only in MVP. Roadmap: hybrid (users can request a source, admin approves → it appears in the public catalog).
**Pros of admin-managed** (what we chose and why):
- One polling job per source = cheap, predictable load.
- We can vet quality / legal / security before exposing a feed.
- Bad URLs / spam is not a problem.
- Limited selection. Power users feel constrained.
- More work for the admin. The roadmap hybrid model addresses this.
- View: alerts, channels, last login, signup date, role.
- Actions: change role, suspend (login blocked, alerts paused), restore, hard delete (with 7-day soft-delete window for accidental clicks).
- **Source status grid**: per source, last fetch time, error rate over last 1h/24h, queue depth.
- **Delivery status**: emails sent / Slack sent, success rate, average latency, error reasons (top 10).
- **Background jobs**: matcher queue depth, oldest unprocessed event age, worker count.
- **Matcher stats**: alerts evaluated/min, matches/min, false-positive feedback (future).
- **Errors**: top 20 application exceptions in the last 24h (structured logs).
This is a one-page view. We use free observability in MVP — structured logs to stdout + a SQLite table for the rolling counters. (Roadmap: OpenTelemetry → free Grafana Cloud or self-host.)

## 3. The safety nets (what we don't let the agent do)
| Push to `main` directly | `pre-tool` hook rejects `git push --force` and direct pushes; we work on branches. |
| Edit `appsettings.Production.json` | `pre-tool` hook rejects writes to that file. |
| Run `dotnet ef database update` against a non-dev connection | `pre-tool` hook inspects the connection string. |
| Skip a failing test | `pre-commit` hook runs `dotnet test --no-build`; commit blocked if any test fails. |
| Hand-edit a migration after it's been merged | `pre-tool` hook rejects edits to `backend/**/Migrations/*.cs`; migrations are owned by the CLI. |
| Add a real secret to the repo | `secrets.instructions.md` + `pre-tool` regex check on common secret patterns. |
| Modify `rbac_policy.csv` silently | `pre-tool` hook rejects; only allowed via a labeled PR. |
| Use a paid data provider | `AGENTS.md` non-negotiable; reviewer agent checks. |
All of these are belt-and-suspenders. The point isn't paranoia; it's that in a 24-hour build, you don't have time to recover from a botched `rm` or a leaked key.

description: 'C# / .NET coding standards for Sonrisa News. Reliability-first rules.'
- **Never `async void`.** Use `async Task` or `async Task<T>`. `void` is allowed only on event handlers, and even then wrap in try/catch.
- **Always pass `CancellationToken`** through async chains. Background services, controllers, and hosted services all have one. Don't drop it.
- **No blocking I/O on async paths.** `Task.Wait`, `Task.Result`, `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` are forbidden in service code (allowed in test setup only).
- **All public methods that touch I/O must be cancellable** AND must observe the token in a loop (so they exit promptly on shutdown).
- **No fire-and-forget tasks** (`_ = SomeMethod()`). Either await it, or queue it in the `IHostedService` lifecycle.
- **Migrations are owned by the CLI.** `dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src/SonrisaNews.Infrastructure`. Never hand-edit `**/Migrations/*.cs`.
- **DbContext is scoped.** One per request in the Api, one per loop iteration in the Worker. Never a singleton.
- **No `IQueryable` returned from a service boundary.** Return `Task<List<T>>` or `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`. The query executes where it's composed.
- **Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only queries.** Default tracking is wasteful in the worker.
- **Use `ExecuteUpdate` / `ExecuteDelete` for bulk operations** when you don't need change tracking.
- **All entity changes go through the `DbContext.SaveChangesAsync(ct)` path.** No raw ADO.NET outside the `Persistence/` layer.
- **No string-typed column comparisons in hot paths.** Use strongly-typed LINQ. If you must use raw SQL, use parameterized queries (no concatenation ever).
- **Every controller action that reads or writes data** must have an `[Authorize(Policy = "…")]` attribute. The policy name is a constant in `Permissions.cs`.

- **The policy name follows the pattern `<Resource>.<Action>.<Scope>`**: e.g. `Alerts.Write.Own`, `Sources.Write.Any`, `Users.Suspend`. The handler in `RbacPolicyHandler.cs` consults Casbin with `(subject, action, resource)`.

- **Resource ownership is enforced at the handler**, not in the controller. The handler reads `currentUser.Id` from the request and passes it as a Casbin domain. Don't repeat ownership checks in the controller body.
- **Admin actions write to `AuditLog`** via the `IAuditLog.RecordAsync(action, target, metadata, ct)` helper. It's called from a filter, not manually.

- **Every action declares `[ProducesResponseType(typeof(TResponse), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]`** AND `[ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]` minimum. Add `401/403/404/409` as relevant.
- **XML doc comments on every public action** with `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`. The OpenAPI doc is the frontend's source of truth.
- **No business logic in controllers.** Controllers parse, validate, call a service, return a result. The service does the work.
- **Use `FluentValidation` for input** (not data annotations). One validator per request DTO. Validator is registered in DI.
- **Never return `Ok(entity)` for entities that contain sensitive fields.** Use a response DTO.
- **`INotificationChannel` implementations** are tested with a fake SMTP / fake HTTP server, never against a real provider. See the `add-a-channel` skill.
- **`IDataSource` implementations** are tested with an injected `HttpMessageHandler` that returns canned responses. No live network in unit tests.
- **All external calls go through a typed `HttpClient`** registered via `AddHttpClient<TClient>(...)`. Don't `new HttpClient()`.

- **Structured properties, not interpolated strings**: `_logger.LogInformation("Alert matched {AlertId} for event {EventId}", alertId, eventId)`, not `LogInformation($"Alert matched {alertId} for event {eventId}")`.
- **Never log a full `payload`** — log the `id` and a short summary. PII is real.
- File-scoped namespaces, `var` for locals, expression-bodied members only when they fit on one line.
- `record` for DTOs and value objects, `class` for entities with identity.
- Primary constructors on .NET 8+ for service classes with simple dependencies.
- Naming: `PascalCase` for types/methods/public members, `_camelCase` for private fields, `I` prefix for interfaces.
- **Named constants over magic numbers**, even single-use. The name is the documentation.
- **No commented-out code. No `#if false` blocks. No "for later" notes in code.** Git has history; the roadmap doc captures intent.
- xUnit + FluentAssertions. One assertion concept per test (multiple `Assert` calls are fine if they verify one behavior).
- **All external services are faked** (no live network, no live SMTP, no live Slack).
- **No real time in tests** — use `IClock` and a fake `ISystemClock`. The `TimeProvider` built into .NET 8+ is acceptable.
## Forbidden patterns (the agent must not introduce these)
- `async void` (except event handlers, and even then wrapped)
- Logging with PII (email, password, full tokens)
- Silent `catch` blocks (always log; re-throw unless you have a deliberate reason)
description: 'EF Core migration rules. Migrations are forward-only and CLI-owned.'
- **Migrations are owned by the EF Core CLI.** The only way to create or modify a migration is:
- **Never hand-edit a migration file** once it's been committed. A `pre-tool` hook blocks edits to `backend/**/Migrations/*.cs`. If you need to change a migration, add a new one.
- Has an `Up` method with a `// Forward-only after merge.` comment as the first line.
- Has a `Down` method (for reference; we don't run `Down` in prod, but it must compile).
- Uses the migration builder API (`migrationBuilder.CreateTable(...)`, `migrationBuilder.AddColumn(...)`, etc.), not raw SQL, unless absolutely necessary.
- If raw SQL is necessary, the `Up` includes the equivalent DDL and the `Down` includes the reverse DDL.
1. **In development**: run `dotnet ef migrations add <Name>` after changing an entity. Commit the new files: `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_<Name>.cs` and the updated `SonrisaNewsModelSnapshot.cs`.
2. **In review**: the reviewer checks the migration diff for accidental drops, dangerous defaults, and missing indexes.
3. **In CI**: a separate `migrations-build` job runs `dotnet ef migrations script --no-build --output migrations.sql` and uploads the SQL artifact for visibility. It does **not** apply.
4. **In prod**: deployment runs `dotnet ef database update` as a pre-start step. Forward-only. No rollback via `Down` — that requires a new migration.
- Adding / removing / renaming an entity property.
- Changing a column type or nullability.
Adding a new entity does **not** require a separate `CreateTable` migration — the `add` command picks it up from the model.
- **Every foreign key gets an index** by default. EF Core does this automatically; verify in the snapshot.
- **Query-hot columns** (e.g. `Event.OccurredAt`, `Match.FiredAt`, `Notification.SentAt`) get an index. Add it via `[Index(nameof(...))]` on the entity.
- **Composite indexes** for the matcher window query: `Event (SourceId, OccurredAt)`. EF generates this from `modelBuilder.Entity<Event>().HasIndex(...)`.
- **Don't rename a column in a migration.** Add the new column, backfill it, deploy, then add a *second* migration to drop the old column. Two migrations are better than one breaking deploy.
- **Don't change a column type** without a `// TODO: backfill` comment in the migration and a follow-up migration to remove the backfill code.
- **Don't drop a table** that has data without a soft-delete intermediate step.
## Forbidden patterns (the agent must not introduce these)
- `migrationBuilder.DropColumn(...)` without a follow-up "did you mean to?" review note
- `database.Migrate()` in production startup code (use `dotnet ef database update` as a pre-start step)
- Custom `IMigration` implementations (the scaffolder's output is the only migration type we use)
- Direct edits to `SonrisaNewsModelSnapshot.cs` (the scaffolder owns it)
description: 'Next.js / React / TypeScript coding standards for Sonrisa News.'
- Next.js 16 App Router. React 19. TypeScript **strict**. MUI v9.
- TanStack Query v5 for client state. React Hook Form + Zod for forms.
- No Tailwind. No shadcn. No Chakra. **MUI only.**
- **Default to Server Components.** Add `'use client'` only when the component needs state, effects, event handlers, browser APIs, or third-party client-only libraries.
- **Push `'use client'` to the leaf.** A wrapper with state, a `<form>` that uses `useForm`, a button with `(onClick)`. Don't mark a whole page client-side just because one child needs it.

- **Never import server-only modules from a client component.** `fs`, `path`, `next/headers`, `next/cookies`, server-only secrets, etc. are off-limits on the client. Use the `server-only` package to make this a build error.
- **Data fetching**: Server Components fetch directly. Client components use `useQuery`. Don't mix the two (Server Component fetches, then passes data to a Client Component via props).
- **`sx` prop for dynamic styles.** `style={{}}` is forbidden when the value is computed at runtime.
- **Theme tokens, not hard-coded values.** `theme.spacing(2)`, `theme.palette.primary.main`, never `'#1976d2'` or `'16px'` in component code.
- **One `<ThemeProvider>` at the root** of `(app)`, `(admin)`, and `(auth)` route groups. Don't nest.
- **No inline `style={{}}` with static values** — use `sx` consistently.
- **`useTheme()` is fine**; reading `theme` from context in the same component is preferred over passing it down.
- **Iconify or `@mui/icons-material`** for icons. Don't import random SVG files.
- React Hook Form + Zod schema, colocated. Schema lives next to the form, e.g. `SignUpForm.tsx` + `signUpSchema.ts`.
- **One Zod schema per form.** Reuse via `z.infer<typeof schema>` for the form's input/output types.
- **Server errors come back typed.** Map the API's `ProblemDetails` (RFC 7807) to a Zod issue, display with `<FormHelperText error>`.
- **No `defaultValues` from props without memoization.** Pass them through `useMemo` or use `values` from a parent query.
- **Query keys are tuples, hierarchical**: `['alerts', alertId, 'history']`. Invalidation: `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['alerts'] })`.
- **No `refetchOnWindowFocus` globally off** unless the data is large and stale is fine. Default is on.
- **Mutations invalidate the smallest set of queries possible.** Don't blast `['alerts']` if you only need `['alerts', alertId]`.
- **Loading states are explicit.** `if (isPending) return <Skeleton />`. No spinners unless the operation is user-initiated.
- **Error states are explicit.** Render `<Alert severity="error">` with a retry button. Never `console.error` and render `null`.
- Access token in memory (Zustand or React context). Refresh token in an httpOnly cookie (set by the backend).
- **`fetch` wrapper intercepts 401 once**, calls `/auth/refresh`, retries the original request. If refresh fails, redirect to sign-in.
- `pnpm --dir web generate:api` regenerates types from the backend's Swagger doc. Run this on every backend change.
- **The client is committed.** Drift is a build error in CI (a separate job compares the committed client to a fresh regeneration and fails if they differ).
- **Use `openapi-fetch` for requests, not raw `fetch`.** Types come for free.
- **Named exports only.** No `export default`. Components, hooks, utilities — all named.
- **No `useEffect` for data fetching.** Use `useQuery`. `useEffect` is for side effects on prop changes (rare).
- **No `useMemo` / `useCallback` "just in case".** Only when there's a measured or obvious reason.
- **No barrel files** (`index.ts` re-exports). Direct imports: `import { Foo } from '@/features/alerts/Foo'`.
- **File size**: ~300 lines max. Extract when approaching the limit.
- Vitest + Testing Library for unit. Playwright for e2e.
- **Test behavior, not implementation.** Don't assert internal state; assert the rendered output or the API call.
- **No real network in unit tests.** Use `msw` to mock the OpenAPI client.
- **No real time** without a controllable clock. Use `vi.useFakeTimers()`.
- Every form input has a `<label>` (use MUI's `<TextField label="…">`).
- Every interactive element is keyboard-reachable in document order.
- Color contrast meets WCAG AA (the default MUI theme does).
## Forbidden patterns (the agent must not introduce these)
- `console.log` in production code (use a logger if you really need one)
- `// @ts-ignore` (use `// @ts-expect-error` with a reason, or fix the type)
- Tailwind, shadcn, Chakra, or any UI library other than MUI

description: 'RBAC rules. The authorization policy file is the security boundary.'

- `Admin` — can manage data sources, users, announcements, system health. Audit-logged on every action.
- `System` — internal role for background workers. Cannot sign in.

| `Alerts.Read.Own` | User, Admin | User can read their own alerts; Admin can read any. |
# Resource, Action, Scope → which roles are allowed
- `*` is a wildcard for the role section (Admin gets everything).
- `g` (grouping) lines assign users to roles. The user identity is the email, not the user id (we want stable identifiers).
- **The file is plain CSV, not YAML, not JSON.** Comments start with `#`.
**Any change to `rbac_policy.csv` or any file in `backend/**/Auth/` must include:**
1. **A unit test that demonstrates the new permission works** for an authorized user.
2. **A unit test that demonstrates the new permission is rejected** for an unauthorized user.

- A new permission constant is added to `Permissions.cs`. It must be granted to at least one role in the policy file.
Use the [`rbac-audit`](../../skills/rbac-audit/SKILL.md) skill to verify there's no drift.
1. Reads the current user from the `HttpContext` (via `ICurrentUser`).
2. Reads the requested permission from the policy attribute.
3. Builds a Casbin request: `(sub=email, obj=resource, act=action, dom=scope)`.
5. On `false`, returns a 403 with a typed problem detail (RFC 7807).

- A role check that bypasses the policy handler (e.g. `if (user.IsAdmin)` in business logic)
- Storing the user's role in the JWT (the role is in the DB, the JWT carries the email, Casbin resolves)
- An `Admin` action that doesn't write to `AuditLog`
- Hard-coded role names in code (always use the `Roles` constants from `Auth/Roles.cs`)
description: 'Secrets rules. No real secrets in the repo, ever.'
Anything that grants access to a system on behalf of the project:
- API keys (SMTP password, Resend key, SendGrid key, Slack webhook URLs)
- Any URL with a username + password in it
- Public OAuth client IDs (these are public by design)
- Email addresses (PII, but not a secret in the threat model)
